threads.body: [Testing] These new AMQP handoff tasks are dependencies of `check`, but selected instrumentation CI runs the explicit task lists in `.github/scripts/instrumentations.sh`. None of the new tasks appears there, and the retry regression is also guarded by `testLatestDeps()`, so it never runs in that matrix. Add the new handoff variants to the regular instrumentation task list and add the required handoff task variants to `TEST_LATEST_DEPS_INSTRUMENTATIONS` so the retry path executes with latest dependencies.

threads.body: [General] `find(...)` treats any active invocation with the same message object and channel as a duplicate interceptor callback. A handler can legitimately call `channel.send(message)` with that same immutable message; the nested `preSend` then adds only a no-op callback, so it reuses the outer processing scope and emits no nested process span or metric. Distinguish duplicate interceptor registration from a reentrant send, and add a regression test that redispatches the same message instance.

threads.body: [General] This still classifies a reentrant `DirectChannel` send of the handler's exact `Message` instance as a duplicate interceptor callback. Direct channels never invoke `beforeHandle`, so the outer send invocation remains the last callback owner; `find(...)` matches its `outputMessage`, this condition succeeds, and the nested send emits no Process span or metric. The new same-message regression only exercises `ExecutorSubscribableChannel`, whose handler callback changes the owner and therefore does not cover this path. Please distinguish callback re-entry from a handler-initiated send for synchronous channels and add the corresponding DirectChannel regression.
